Sourced Statements: The layoffs were expected after Meta told employees in April that the reductions would begin May 20.
Notifications began in Asia before spreading to Europe and the United States, according to Bloomberg.
Meta, which owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has framed the cuts as part of a broader push to make the company more efficient while it spends heavily on AI.

In January, the company told investors it expected 2026 capital expenditures of $115 billion to $135 billion, with growth driven by investments to support Meta Superintelligence Labs and its core business. Meta reported $200.97 billion in revenue and $60.46 billion in net income for 2025.
The New York Times reported Wednesday that some employees had signed petitions opposing a Meta program that would use employee data to train internal Al tools.
The Times also reported that workers exchanged messages remotely and checked internal directories to learn which colleagues had been cut.
Reuters reported that Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg told employees he did not expect more company-wide layoffs this year, according to an internal memo the news agency reviewed.
The company has said in past restructuring statements that teams regularly make changes to align resources with their goals.
